# Weightless Neural Networks --- From Language Modeling to Network Security

This research explores **Weightless Neural Networks** (WNNs) --- specifically RAM-based neurons --- as a foundation for machine learning tasks that demand O(1) inference, sub-kilobyte models, and real-time adaptability.

## Current Focus

**[Network Intrusion Detection on FPGA](posts/20260309-week16.qmd)** --- exploiting the WNN's structural advantages for line-rate packet classification:

- **O(1) inference**: RAM lookup in a single clock cycle (~5ns on FPGA) --- classify *every* packet at 100Gbps
- **O(1) online learning**: Single memory write updates the model --- adapt to new threats in real-time
- **Sub-kilobyte models**: 192 bytes demonstrated [@santiago2020fpga] --- fits in FPGA block RAM
- **[Connectivity optimization](optimization-methods.qmd#phased-search)**: [GA](optimization-methods.qmd#genetic-algorithm) [@holland1975adaptation; @goldberg1989genetic] + [TS](optimization-methods.qmd#tabu-search) [@glover1989tabu1; @glover1990tabu2] over neuron connectivity patterns
- **[Rust+Metal acceleration](posts/20251229-week4.qmd#rustmetal-accelerator)**: Full pipeline on Apple Silicon (16 CPU + 40 GPU cores)

Secondary direction: **Edge AI / TinyML** for battery-powered sensors (predictive maintenance, HAR) [@susskind2021nanoml].

## Phase 1: Language Modeling (Weeks 1--15)

We spent 15 weeks building a complete RAM-based language model on WikiText-2. The honest conclusion: **RAM WNNs are structurally disadvantaged for precise probability estimation over large vocabularies** ([full analysis](posts/20260309-week15.qmd#analysis-why-the-wnn-model-barely-contributes)). The optimal interpolation mixture assigns 0% weight to the WNN model.

*All models evaluated on WikiText-2 with GPT-2 tokenizer (50,257 vocab).
CE = [Cross-Entropy](posts/20251229-week4.qmd#evaluation-metrics),
PPL = [Perplexity](posts/20251229-week4.qmd#evaluation-metrics),
Acc = [top-1 accuracy](posts/20251229-week4.qmd#evaluation-metrics).*

| Architecture | CE | PPL | Acc | Details |
